analysis.title: US Daily: What Does the Tightening in Financial Conditions Mean for Growth and the Fed?
key_insights: GS Financial Conditions Index has tightened about 100bp this year, all of it since early September, with over 40bp coming in the last week alone.
Main contributors are the rise in interest rates over the year, the recent decline in equity prices and dollar appreciation.
If the tightening persists, GS estimates a 0.5pp drag on 2026Q4 GDP growth and 0.5pp on 2027 Q4/Q4 growth, a few tenths more than implied by the 2027 forecast of 2.4% GDP growth.
If GS strategists' 2027 forecasts prove right, with equities rebounding and long-term rates falling, more than half of the tightening reverses and there is no additional growth drag next year.
A second 25bp hike in December is a near certainty, and GS continues to expect a third hike in March.
Reason one for the March hike: the tightening equals the usual impact of 100bp of hikes, and most FOMC participants likely envision 75-100bp of total hikes, so it is not disproportionate to intent.
Reason two: part of the tightening is higher long-term rates driven by expectations of more hikes, which could reverse if the FOMC does not follow through.
Reason three: unlike early 2016 and late 2018, inflation is high and growth is a bit above potential, so participants worry less that hikes do more harm than good.
Some FOMC participants could project fewer hikes in the December dot plot because of the tightening.
Further tightening led by deteriorating risk sentiment, especially an equity selloff on AI spending concerns, could displace hikes next year because AI demand is boosting core PCE inflation.
Equities contribute to FCI tightening despite a roughly flat S&P 500 because they enter as a price-earnings ratio using a ten-year average of earnings that has risen.

risk_factors: Further FCI tightening driven by risk sentiment deterioration that persists independent of hike expectations.
Equity selloff tied to concerns about a pullback in AI spending could displace rate hikes.
Long-term rates reversing if the FOMC does not follow through on hikes expected by markets.
Persistent tightening could drag growth by an extra few tenths versus the baseline.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 left plots the GS US FCI from Jan-26 to Oct-26, and the right panel shows change in FCI and components since start of 2026, with the FCI up about 104.1bp in the labeled figure.
Exhibit 2 shows the real GDP growth impulse from the GS FCI under three paths: FCI stays at the Nov. 19 level, FCI follows GS strategy forecasts, and FCI at the October FOMC level.
geopolitical: The FCI tightened meaningfully when the Iran war began but then quickly reversed and was unchanged for the year as of early September.

tension_points.bull_case: Hikes continue because the tightening is in line with the 75-100bp of hikes participants intend, and inflation is high with growth above potential, so GS expects a third hike in March.
tension_points.bear_case: Further tightening from weaker risk sentiment or an AI-driven equity selloff could persuade the FOMC that more hikes are unnecessary.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further tightening led by risk sentiment deterioration or AI spending concerns that persists independent of hike expectations, or a lower dot plot in December.
